message.content:
Below is a ready‑to‑use **curl** command (and a short Python snippet) that will fetch only the `id` and `context` fields for community comments on the domain `test4.org`.  
It uses the continuation cursor `cur456` and your API key `key123`.

---

## 1. REST‑style request (curl)

```bash
curl -X GET "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/domains/test4.org/community/comments" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer key123" \
     -H "Accept: application/json" \
     -G \
     --data-urlencode "fields=id,context" \
     --data-urlencode "cursor=cur456"
```

### What each part does

| Part | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `https://api.yourservice.com/v1/domains/test4.org/community/comments` | Endpoint for community comments on the specified domain. |
| `-H "Authorization: Bearer key123"` | Passes your API key in the Authorization header. |
| `-H "Accept: application/json"` | Requests JSON output. |
| `-G` | Tells curl to send the data as query parameters (GET). |
| `--data-urlencode "fields=id,context"` | Instructs the API to return only the `id` and `context` fields. |
| `--data-urlencode "cursor=cur456"` | Supplies the continuation cursor so the API returns the next page. |

> **Tip:** If your API uses a different base URL or path, replace `https://api.yourservice.com/v1` with the correct one.

---

## 2. Python example (requests)

```python
import requests

url = "https://api.yourservice.com/v1/domains/test4.org/community/comments"
headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer key123",
    "Accept": "application/json",
}
params = {
    "fields": "id,context",
    "cursor": "cur456",
}

response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
response.raise_for_status()          # Raises an error for bad status codes
data = response.json()

print(data)   # Contains only id and context for each comment
```

---

### Expected JSON structure

```json
{
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": "cmt001",
      "context": { /* context object */ }
    },
    {
      "id": "cmt002",
      "context": { /* context object */ }
    }
    // …
  ],
  "next_cursor": "cur789"   // if more pages exist
}
```

Feel free to adjust the field names (`fields`, `cursor`) if your API uses different query‑parameter names. Happy querying!
